summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with bare-metal embedded firmware experience on ARM Cortex-M (STM32) microcontrollers, building real-time control loops around high-resolution PWM generation, high-speed ADC sampling, and hardware timers. Skilled in UART/I2C/SPI peripheral drivers, FreeRTOS multi-task coordination, and hardware debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG/SWD. Experienced integrating embedded C/C++ firmware with networked infrastructure and CMake/Git-based build workflows.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi over I2C and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and timing/resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built bare-metal embedded C firmware on an ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32) microcontroller with timer-triggered high-speed ADC sampling and interrupt-driven capture for real-time sensing.
Programmed microcontroller peripherals directly (GPIO, TIM2 hardware timers, ADC1, I2C1), achieving a deterministic 1 Hz update rate within 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM.
Verified timing and signal integrity in Proteus and with an oscilloscope prior to hardware bring-up.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo, high-resolution PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override on an ARM Cortex-M (STM32) target.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory multi-task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Deployed the Jetson-side controller as a systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation) with static IP networking over Ethernet for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
